source.title: The Age of Reason: Functional Brain Network Development during Childhood

confidence_rationale: Empirical fMRI study (ages 4-10) that directly challenges the strict back-to-front reading INV-088 leans on: it finds pronounced development at BOTH ends of the sensory-association gradient, not sensory-first-then-association. This weakens any claim that the world-representation must fully differentiate before the evaluator begins maturing. However, INV-088's actual assertion is a functional BOUND (evaluator quality bounded by differentiation), which is compatible with concurrent co-development so long as the bound holds -- so the study is a genuine caveat on the ordering premise rather than a refutation of the bound. Logged 'mixed' at moderate confidence because it is a real, well-powered counter-signal on the timing story while not measuring the bound itself.
failure_signatures: Development was pronounced at both the perceptual (visual) and abstract (medial prefrontal) ends of the sensory-association gradient in 4-10 year olds, contradicting the classical view -- which INV-088's ordering premise invokes -- that sensory areas develop first and association areas last.

The study measures functional network segregation/integration, not evaluator readout quality as a function of representational differentiation, so it can neither confirm nor refute the causal bound; it only removes strict temporal precedence as supporting evidence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In children aged 4-10, age is associated with increasing segregation between externally-oriented perceptual systems and internally-oriented abstract systems, with pronounced functional development at BOTH ends of the sensory-association gradient -- challenging the classical theory that cortical maturation proceeds strictly back-to-front (sensory first, association last).
mapping.ree_translation: INV-088 leans on a sensory-before-evaluator ordering (z_world differentiates, then the evaluator can be productively trained). Tooley et al. show that in early childhood both the perceptual (z_world-like) and abstract/evaluative (E3-like) ends develop concurrently and prominently, so strict temporal precedence of world-representation over evaluator is not a safe assumption. The bound INV-088 asserts can still hold under concurrent development -- but the developmental-timing argument for it is weakened.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a caveat on the ordering premise, not a test of the functional bound. INV-088 does not strictly require sensory to finish before the evaluator starts; it requires evaluator quality to track differentiation. Concurrent maturation at both ends is consistent with a live bound. Reading this as a hard refutation would over-claim; reading it as no-signal would be dishonest.
mapping.source_context: Human task-free fMRI functional connectivity, N~92 children ages 4-10, advanced pediatric acquisition; graph-theoretic network segregation measures.

confidence_components.notes: Strong methods on a hard-to-scan population (J Neurosci). Mapping fidelity 0.55: it targets the ordering premise, not the bound. Direction 'mixed' -- it weakens strict precedence while leaving the functional bound untouched; kept as an explicit balance against the two supporting developmental anchors.
